title: Classicality is Zariski local
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a discrete commutative ring and $F$ a
$\Lambda_X$-module sheaf on $X_{\Proet}$. If $X=\bigcup_aX_a$ is an open covering
such that each restriction $F|_{X_a}$ is classical on $(X_a)_{\Proet}$, then $F$ is
classical. Conversely the restriction of a classical sheaf to an open subscheme
is classical.

proof.text:
First justify restriction compatibility. For an open $U\subset X$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] and [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identify its two sites with the respective slice sites and identify the restricted pro-étale coefficient ring with $\Lambda_U$. For an étale sheaf $E$ on $X$ and $W	o U$ pro-étale, the presheaf-colimit formula of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] identifies the two presheaf pullbacks: replace each pair $(T,W	o T)$ with $(T	imes_XU,W	o T	imes_XU)$ and each section $s\in E(T)$ with its restriction. Inclusion of pairs étale over $U$ is the inverse on colimits, since $T	imes_XU	o T$ supplies the relation identifying these representatives. The coverings and their refinements over every such $W$ are the same in the slice and the original site; hence the two plus constructions of [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-plus-theorem] show that sheafification commutes with this restriction. The resulting natural identification $(
u_X^*E)|_U\cong
u_U^*(E|_U)$ respects addition and scalar action, since it is defined by restriction of sections. If $F$ is classical, [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] gives $F\cong
u_X^*E$ for an étale module sheaf $E$; the displayed identification and the same node for $U$ prove that $F|_U$ is classical.

source.place: First sentence: inverse image commutes with restriction to open subschemes.

proof.text:
Assume the restrictions to an open cover $X= igcup_aX_a$ are classical. By [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], choose a $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F_a$ on $(X_a)_{\Et}$ and an isomorphism $\alpha_a:
u_{X_a}^*F_a\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_{X_a}$ for each $a$. On $X_{ab}=X_a\cap X_b$, functoriality of restriction identifies the restriction of $\alpha_b^{-1}\alpha_a$ with a map $
u_{X_{ab}}^*(F_a|_{X_{ab}})	o
u_{X_{ab}}^*(F_b|_{X_{ab}})$. The full-faithfulness clause of [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] gives a unique $\Lambda$-linear isomorphism $\varphi_{ab}:F_a|_{X_{ab}}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_b|_{X_{ab}}$ lifting it. On triple overlaps the two composites have the same image under $
u^*$, so faithfulness gives $\varphi_{bc}\circ\varphi_{ab}=\varphi_{ac}$; the diagonal maps are identities by uniqueness applied to $\alpha_a^{-1}\alpha_a=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Choice of local models and overlap cocycle.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing] to the étale site of $X$ with final object $X$, the covering family of open immersions $X_a\to X$, the constant ring sheaf $\Lambda$, the local module sheaves $F_a$, and the transition isomorphisms $\varphi_{ab}$. The slice identification from step 1 identifies the local module categories. Since coverings on an object over $X_a$ are unchanged, the same plus-construction argument from step 1 applied to the constant ring presheaf identifies the restricted constant étale ring sheaf with the one on $X_a$, including all ring operations. Its fibre products are the overlap schemes $X_{ab}$, and its cocycle hypothesis, including repeated indices, is the identity from step 2. We obtain an étale module sheaf $F_0$ and linear isomorphisms $e_a:F_0|_{X_a}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_a$ satisfying $\varphi_{ab}e_a=e_b$ on overlaps.

source.place: Étale sheaves glue along Zariski coverings.

proof.text:
Set $ eta_a=\alpha_a\circ
u^*(e_a)$ using step 1's natural restriction identification. On $X_{ab}$ the two overlap equations give $ eta_a=\alpha_a
u^*e_a=\alpha_b
u^*\varphi_{ab}
u^*e_a=\alpha_b
u^*e_b= eta_b$. The Zariski cover is a pro-étale cover by [sk-def-pe-site]. Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] to the pro-étale site of $X$, its final object $X$, ring $\Lambda_X$, and module sheaves $
u_X^*F_0,F$. All overlap fibre products exist as scheme fibre products; step 1 identifies the slice restrictions and coefficients. It gives a unique linear map $ eta:
u_X^*F_0	o F$ with these local restrictions. Since equal isomorphisms have equal inverses, the $ eta_a^{-1}$ agree on overlaps and the same lemma glues them to $\gamma:F	o
u_X^*F_0$. The composites $\gamma eta$ and $ eta\gamma$ restrict to the identity maps, so uniqueness in that lemma makes them identities globally. Thus $F\cong
u_X^*F_0$ is classical by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules].

source.place: The local isomorphisms glue to an isomorphism $\nu_X^*F_0\cong F$.
